thread:
jess: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about doing an ingress-side prevalidation that runs model-specific tokenization to early-reject requests that will exceed the model token window. The idea is to fail fast with guidance rather than let expensive partial streams happen. Thoughts?

dmitri: interesting. what's the main win? cost or UX?

jess: both. cost: avoid wasted GPU cycles on requests that will be aborted mid-stream. UX: return a clear rejection with suggested truncation or alternate model. Also avoids billing surprises for customers who estimated tokens differently.

kira: risky area: our tokenizers aren't perfectly stable across model variants/quantizations. If edge uses a slightly different tokenizer than runtime we could false-positive reject. How do we keep them in sync?

jess: good point. plan A: use the same tokenizer library bundle that we ship with runtime (same code path) but run a lightweight wasm tokenizer at edge. Plan B: fallback to a conservative heuristic if tokenizer bundle not available (estimate > actual -> allow).

sam: what about streaming semantics? if we reject at ingress we avoid streaming entirely. But some callers rely on partial outputs even if full request fails.

jess: tradeoff. We could offer two modes: strict (deny if over) and permissive (start stream and stream a header warning). But permissive reintroduces the waste we tried to avoid.

dmitri: also think about retries and idempotency. If client auto-retries after 413, we must surface a stable rejection code + hint. Otherwise we end up with retry storms.

kira: agree. propose to use 413 with Retry-After and an X-Edge-Token-Estimate header and an idempotency advisory. Example:

```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Retry-After: 60
X-Edge-Token-Estimate: 6120
X-Edge-Max-Tokens: 4096
Body: {"suggestion": "truncate prompt or use /dedicated for larger windows"}
```

sam: can the client use that to auto-truncate? mobile SDKs might want a helper.

jess: yep, we'll surface a structured error code in the API SDKs. Also include a suggested truncation point when we can compute it cheaply.

infra-bot: note: this requires the edge to carry model metadata (max_tokens + tokenizer hash). storage cost ~ small; we also need an update path when models roll.

dmitri: update path is the tricky bit. we cannot block edge deploys for every model change. propose a catalog version header and delta pulls. edge will have a default TTL for tokenizer bundles. When TTL expired, requests can still be served using conservative heuristics.

kira: what's conservative? we could multiply client estimate by 1.3 or add 10% headroom. But that weakens the benefit.

jess: we accept some false-negatives (allowing some oversized requests) but minimize false-positives (rejecting good requests). false-positives are worse for developer trust.

rate-limit-bot: reminder: rejecting at ingress should count against rate quotas? we should decide whether 413s consume tokens/quota. Current billing path charges on tokens consumed at runtime only.

dmitri: I think ingress rejects should not count as usage. They did not make it to runtime. But we should count them against request rate quotas to avoid abuse.

sam: edge-case: clients passing an alternate model param mid-stream or switching to a smaller model in retries. We must ensure idempotency keys and retry hints survive.

jess: plan: include X-Edge-Supports-Prevalidate and X-Edge-Token-Hash in 200/413 responses to make client decisions deterministic. We'll also add an SDK flag: prevalidate=true|false.

deply-bot: (typo) deploy-bot: feature-flagging: we can roll prevalidation behind a flag per-region and per-customer. safe rollout path: start with a small % of traffic and only for hosted models with stable tokenizer hashes.

kira: metrics to monitor: false-positive rate, rejected-by-model, downstream failed starts, retry storms. Also track avg latency added at edge for tokenization.

jess: agreed. action items: i'll draft an RFC with: tokenizer bundle sync plan, headers spec (X-Edge-Token-Estimate, X-Edge-Token-Hash, X-Edge-Max-Tokens), error body shape, and feature-flag rollout. dmitri: prototype wasm tokenizer at edge. kira: validate SDK ergonomics for auto-truncation + deterministic retry behavior. sam: check implications for streaming SDKs that expect partial output.

dmitri: I can have a spike by EOD Friday.

kira: i'll inventory SDKs and list which need helper methods.

jess: cool. thanks all. :thumbsup:
